mechanism_variables: Sympathetic reactivity index (SRI): normalized peak EDA phasic driver amplitude during TSST relative to baseline
HRV reactivity index: log(RMSSD_baseline / RMSSD_TSST)
Conformity score quantile: empirical quantile of nonconformity scores for true class in calibration set
Coverage indicator: binary (1 if true label in prediction set, 0 otherwise)
mechanism_builds.causal_path: High SRI → shifted conditional feature distribution p(X|Y=stress) → conformity scores from calibration (lower SRI) underestimate test nonconformity → prediction intervals too narrow → undercoverage for high-SRI subjects
mechanism_builds.expected_direction: Positive correlation between SRI and undercoverage magnitude (higher SRI → lower coverage)
domain_specific_boundary_conditions: WESAD protocol: TSST as sole psychosocial stressor
Empatica E4 sampling: EDA 4Hz, BVP 64Hz
Mondrian stratification: 3 classes (baseline, stress, amusement)
Calibration set: first 70% of each condition per subject
measurable_outcomes: Per-subject coverage rate for stress class
Calibration vs. test conformity score distribution KS distance stratified by SRI tertile
Conditional coverage given SRI > 75th percentile vs. SRI < 25th percentile
mechanism_builds.mechanism_builder_notes: SRI must be computed from calibration-phase data only to avoid circularity. Use phasic EDA driver (cvxEDA) not raw SCR peaks. HRV reactivity uses RMSSD from 5-min windows. Test coverage computed on held-out 30%.

mechanism_variables: Movement artifact index (MAI): median ACC magnitude (sqrt(x^2+y^2+z^2)) during stress condition
PPG signal quality index (SQI): proportion of 10s windows with kurtosis in [1,5] and spectral entropy > 0.7
EDA tonic drift: slope of EDA tonic component (cvxEDA) over stress condition duration
Stratum-wise conformity score variance: variance of nonconformity scores within Mondrian stress stratum
mechanism_builds.causal_path: High MAI → sensor-skin gap modulation → PPG/EDA signal corruption → feature distribution shift between calibration (low MAI) and test (high MAI) → inflated conformity score variance → quantile overestimation → undercoverage
mechanism_builds.expected_direction: Positive correlation between MAI and stress-class undercoverage; negative correlation between SQI and coverage
domain_specific_boundary_conditions: Empatica E4 wrist placement: non-dominant wrist
WESAD TSST involves seated speech/math with limited gross movement
ACC range: ±2g, 32Hz
Mondrian strata: protocol-defined conditions only
measurable_outcomes: Per-subject MAI vs. stress coverage correlation (Spearman)
Calibration-test feature distribution MMD (maximum mean discrepancy) for PPG/EDA features vs. MAI
Conformity score variance inflation factor: var_test / var_calibration per subject
mechanism_builds.mechanism_builder_notes: MAI computed from ACC during stress condition only. SQI uses template matching (Orphanidou 2015). Feature set: 12 EDA + 8 HRV + 6 RESP features per 60s window. MMD with RBF kernel bandwidth = median pairwise distance.

mechanism_variables: HRV recovery half-life: time (seconds) for RMSSD to return to 50% of baseline→stress drop during post-stress rest
EDA recovery half-life: time for tonic EDA to decay 50% from stress peak
Inter-trial interval (ITI): WESAD protocol rest duration between conditions (fixed ~5-10 min)
Baseline-class conformity score contamination: proportion of 'baseline' calibration windows with RMSSD < baseline_median - 0.5*stress_drop
mechanism_builds.causal_path: Long recovery half-life > ITI → residual stress physiology in subsequent 'baseline' period → baseline calibration samples contaminated with stress-like features → baseline conformity scores inflated → stress-class prediction intervals narrowed (Mondrian uses per-class quantiles) → stress undercoverage
mechanism_builds.expected_direction: Subjects with recovery half-life > ITI show lower stress coverage; positive correlation between half-life and baseline contamination proportion
domain_specific_boundary_conditions: WESAD condition order: baseline → TSST → amusement → meditation → recovery
ITI between TSST and next baseline-like condition (meditation) ≈ 5 min
HRV computed from 5-min windows with 50% overlap
Mondrian calibration: class-conditional quantiles per stratum
measurable_outcomes: Per-subject HRV/EDA recovery half-life (exponential fit to post-stress decay)
Baseline contamination rate: % of post-TSST 'baseline' windows with stress-like features
Stress coverage vs. recovery half-life (logistic regression)
Calibration baseline conformity score median vs. true baseline (pre-TSST) median
mechanism_builds.mechanism_builder_notes: Fit exponential decay: RMSSD(t) = RMSSD_stress + (RMSSD_baseline - RMSSD_stress)*(1 - exp(-t/tau)). Half-life = tau*ln(2). Use only first post-TSST rest period. Contamination threshold: RMSSD < baseline_median - 0.5*(baseline_median - stress_median).

mechanism_variables: Interoceptive accuracy (IA): heartbeat counting task score (Schandry) or heartbeat discrimination AUC if available
Self-report stress label: WESAD questionnaire rating (0-10) per condition
Physiological stress index (PSI): composite z-score of EDA phasic rate, HR, HRV during condition
Label-physiology discrepancy: |self-report - PSI| normalized
mechanism_builds.causal_path: Low IA → high label-physiology discrepancy during calibration → mislabeled calibration points (e.g., true stress labeled baseline) → Mondrian computes conformity scores against wrong class-conditional distribution → prediction intervals miscalibrated for true stress class → undercoverage
mechanism_builds.expected_direction: Negative correlation between IA and stress undercoverage; positive correlation between label-physiology discrepancy and undercoverage
domain_specific_boundary_conditions: WESAD self-report: PANAS + stress questionnaire after each condition
No concurrent interoceptive measure in WESAD; IA must be inferred or from external cohort
Mondrian treats protocol condition labels as ground truth
15 subjects, 3 stress-relevant conditions (TSST, amusement, meditation)
measurable_outcomes: Simulated label noise experiment: inject synthetic mislabels at rates matching observed discrepancy, measure coverage drop
Per-subject label-physiology discrepancy vs. coverage (if IA proxy available)
Conformity score distribution shift when recalibrating with PSI-derived labels vs. protocol labels
mechanism_builds.mechanism_builder_notes: Since WESAD lacks direct IA measure, use PSI-protocol label discrepancy as proxy. PSI = first PC of [EDA_phasic_rate, HR, -logRMSSD, RESP_rate] z-scored per subject. Discrepancy = |questionnaire_stress - PSI|. Simulate mislabeling by flipping labels for windows with discrepancy > threshold.

mechanism_variables: Within-condition stress intensity (WSI): continuous PSI (see H4) during TSST
Trait anxiety: STAI-T score (WESAD includes STAI)
Stratum conformity score distribution: empirical CDF of nonconformity scores for stress class
Subject-specific conformity score shift: median(test_scores) - median(calibration_scores) for stress class
mechanism_builds.causal_path: High trait anxiety → higher WSI for same protocol condition (TSST) → feature distribution shifts toward more extreme stress physiology → test conformity scores exceed calibration quantile (computed from lower-WSI subjects) → undercoverage for high-WSI subjects
mechanism_builds.expected_direction: Positive correlation between WSI (or trait anxiety) and stress-class conformity score shift; negative correlation with coverage
domain_specific_boundary_conditions: WESAD: single TSST exposure per subject
STAI-T available for all 15 subjects
Mondrian stress stratum pools all TSST windows across subjects
Calibration: 70% of TSST windows per subject
measurable_outcomes: WSI vs. stress coverage correlation (Spearman)
Conformity score shift vs. WSI (linear regression)
Stratum-wise conformity score CDF separation: high-WSI (top 33%) vs. low-WSI (bottom 33%) subjects
Coverage when re-stratifying by WSI tertile vs. protocol label
mechanism_builds.mechanism_builder_notes: WSI = mean PSI during TSST. PSI as defined in H4. Trait anxiety = STAI-T. Test conformity score shift computed on held-out 30% TSST windows. Re-stratification experiment: bin subjects by WSI tertile, compute Mondrian per bin, compare coverage.

mechanism_variables: Recording time: clock time of WESAD session start (metadata)
Circadian phase proxy: hours from habitual wake time (estimated from baseline HRV)
Baseline sympathetic tone: EDA tonic level + HR during pre-TSST baseline
Stratum exchangeability violation: MMD between baseline-class feature distributions for morning vs. evening subjects
mechanism_builds.causal_path: Late recording time → advanced circadian phase → higher baseline sympathetic tone → baseline feature distribution shifts toward stress distribution → Mondrian baseline stratum mixes circadian states → stress-class quantile contaminated by circadian-shifted baseline scores → stress undercoverage for evening subjects
mechanism_builds.expected_direction: Evening-recorded subjects (after 14:00) show lower stress coverage; positive correlation between recording time and baseline sympathetic tone
domain_specific_boundary_conditions: WESAD recording times: range ~09:00-17:00 (per metadata)
Circadian cortisol peak ~30-45 min post-wake; autonomic follows similar rhythm
Mondrian baseline stratum: all pre-TSST baseline windows pooled
No time-of-day covariate in Mondrian stratification
measurable_outcomes: Recording time vs. baseline EDA tonic / HR correlation
Morning (before 12:00) vs. evening (after 14:00) stress coverage comparison
MMD between morning/evening baseline feature distributions
Coverage when adding time-of-day as stratification variable
mechanism_builds.mechanism_builder_notes: Use WESAD metadata for recording start time. Baseline sympathetic tone = mean EDA tonic (cvxEDA) + mean HR over 5-min pre-TSST baseline. MMD with RBF kernel on 26-dim feature vector. Morning/evening split at median recording time.

mechanism_variables: High-order interaction features: EDA_phasic × HRV_RMSSD × RESP_phase (binned)
Subject-specific interaction weight: coefficient from subject-wise logistic regression (stress vs. baseline) using interaction terms
Marginal vs. conditional conformity score variance: var(scores|label) vs. var(scores|label, interaction_tertile)
Calibration representativeness: KL divergence between calibration and test conformity score distributions within stress stratum
mechanism_builds.causal_path: Subject-heterogeneous feature interactions → true conformity score distribution depends on interaction state → marginal stratification (label only) averages over interaction states → calibration scores non-representative for test samples with different interaction profile → quantile miscalibration → undercoverage for subjects with rare interaction profiles
mechanism_builds.expected_direction: Subjects with high interaction weight magnitude show larger calibration-test conformity score KL divergence and lower coverage
domain_specific_boundary_conditions: Feature set: 26 features (12 EDA, 8 HRV, 6 RESP) per 60s window
Interaction terms: 3-way products of z-scored key features (EDA_phasic, RMSSD, RESP_rate)
Mondrian: no interaction conditioning
15 subjects → limited calibration samples per interaction state
measurable_outcomes: Per-subject interaction weight (logistic regression coefficient for top interaction term)
KL divergence: calibration vs. test conformity scores within stress stratum per subject
Coverage vs. interaction weight correlation
Coverage improvement when using interaction-aware stratification (e.g., k-means on interaction features)
mechanism_builds.mechanism_builder_notes: Compute interaction features as element-wise product of z-scored EDA_phasic_driver, logRMSSD, RESP_rate. Fit subject-wise logistic regression (stress vs. baseline) with main effects + 3-way interaction. Weight = interaction coefficient. KL divergence estimated via k-nearest neighbors (k=5) on conformity scores.

mechanism_variables: Physiological phenotype cluster: k-means (k=4) on subject-level stress response features (mean PSI, EDA/HRV ratio, recovery slope)
Effective calibration size per phenotype: n_calibration_windows for subject's phenotype within stress stratum
Quantile estimation error: |empirical_quantile(0.9) - true_quantile(0.9)| via bootstrap
Phenotype rarity: proportion of total calibration windows belonging to subject's phenotype
mechanism_builds.causal_path: Rare phenotype (e.g., parasympathetic-dominant) → small effective calibration subset within stress stratum → high-variance empirical quantile → systematic downward bias (order statistic bias) → prediction intervals too narrow → undercoverage for rare-phenotype subjects
mechanism_builds.expected_direction: Negative correlation between effective calibration size and coverage; rare phenotypes (frequency < 15%) show largest quantile bias and undercoverage
domain_specific_boundary_conditions: WESAD: 15 subjects, ~300 stress windows total, ~210 calibration
Phenotype clustering on subject-level aggregates (not window-level)
Mondrian stress stratum: all TSST windows pooled
Target coverage: 90% (alpha=0.1)
measurable_outcomes: Phenotype frequency distribution across 15 subjects
Per-phenotype effective calibration size vs. coverage
Bootstrap quantile bias: mean(empirical_q90 - true_q90) per phenotype (true_q90 from pooled bootstrap)
Coverage when using phenotype-stratified Mondrian vs. standard
mechanism_builds.mechanism_builder_notes: Phenotype features: [mean_PSI_TSST, EDA_phasic/HRV_ratio, HRV_recovery_slope]. K=4 clusters (GMM). Effective size = sum of calibration windows from subjects in same cluster. Bootstrap: resample calibration windows 1000x, compute 90th percentile each time, bias = mean(boot_q90) - pooled_q90.

mechanism_variables: Skin temperature change: ΔT = T_wrist_stress - T_wrist_baseline (Empatica E4 thermistor)
EDA baseline shift: ΔEDA_tonic = tonic_stress - tonic_baseline (cvxEDA)
EDA gain change: ΔEDA_phasic_per_stimulus = (phasic_rate_stress / SCR_count_stress) - (phasic_rate_baseline / SCR_count_baseline)
Thermoregulatory response type: vasoconstriction (ΔT < -0.5°C) vs. vasodilation (ΔT > 0.5°C) vs. stable
mechanism_builds.causal_path: Stress → subject-specific thermoregulatory response (vasoconstriction/dilation) → skin temperature change at wrist → EDA baseline/gain shift (temperature-dependent sweat gland conductance) → EDA feature distribution shift between calibration (baseline temp) and test (stress temp) → conformity score miscalibration → undercoverage for large |ΔT| subjects
mechanism_builds.expected_direction: Subjects with |ΔT| > 0.5°C show lower stress coverage; ΔT correlates with EDA baseline shift magnitude
domain_specific_boundary_conditions: Empatica E4 thermistor: 0.1°C resolution, 4Hz, wrist skin temperature
EDA temperature coefficient: ~5-10% per °C (literature)
WESAD: baseline → TSST transition ~5 min
Mondrian: EDA features computed per 60s window, no temperature correction
measurable_outcomes: ΔT vs. stress coverage correlation
ΔT vs. ΔEDA_tonic correlation (per subject)
Calibration-test EDA feature MMD vs. |ΔT|
Coverage when adding temperature as covariate in conformity score (e.g., temperature-normalized EDA)
mechanism_builds.mechanism_builder_notes: ΔT = median(T_last_5min_TSST) - median(T_last_5min_baseline). EDA tonic from cvxEDA. Phasic rate = SCR peaks/min. SCR detection: threshold 0.01 μS. Temperature normalization: EDA_corrected = EDA_raw * exp(-k*(T - T_ref)) with k=0.07/°C (Boucsein 2012).

mechanism_variables: Trait anxiety: STAI-T score (WESAD)
Anticipatory activation index (AAI): (HR_baseline - HR_rest) / (HR_TSST - HR_rest) where HR_rest = first 2 min of recording
Baseline conformity score contamination: proportion of baseline windows with conformity score > stress-class median
Stress-class prediction interval width: 90th percentile of stress calibration conformity scores
mechanism_builds.causal_path: High trait anxiety → anticipatory activation during nominal baseline (high AAI) → baseline conformity scores resemble stress scores → Mondrian baseline stratum inflated → stress-class quantile computed from contaminated baseline (Mondrian uses all classes for normalization?) → stress prediction interval narrowed → stress undercoverage for high-anxiety subjects
mechanism_builds.expected_direction: Positive correlation between STAI-T and AAI; positive correlation between AAI and baseline contamination; negative correlation between AAI and stress coverage
domain_specific_boundary_conditions: WESAD: STAI-T available, baseline = 20 min pre-TSST (includes anticipation period)
Mondrian: class-conditional quantiles, but baseline contamination affects stress quantile if conformity score function uses all classes
AAI denominator: HR_TSST - HR_rest (full stress response range)
HR_rest: first 2 min of recording (pre-anticipation)
measurable_outcomes: STAI-T vs. AAI correlation
AAI vs. baseline contamination rate correlation
High-STAI (top 33%) vs. low-STAI (bottom 33%) stress coverage comparison
Coverage when re-labeling high-AAI baseline windows as 'anticipation' stratum
mechanism_builds.mechanism_builder_notes: AAI = (mean_HR_baseline_last_5min - mean_HR_first_2min) / (mean_HR_TSST - mean_HR_first_2min). Baseline contamination: conformity score > median(stress_calibration_scores). Conformity score = 1 - softmax(stress_class) from base classifier. Re-labeling experiment: create 4th stratum for high-AAI baseline windows.
